patches.value: Let D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1]. First show 0≤D≤n<∞. Nonnegativity is part of the critical-exponent definition. If n=0, ℝ⁰ is a singleton and E is that singleton, so D=0. If n>0, compactness H002 implies boundedness: the open cover of E by radius-one balls has a finite subcover, so E lies in a bounded box. For every sufficiently small h>0, subdivide this box into at most C h^(−n) grid cubes, C independent of h, each of diameter ≤√n h. For every fixed real m>n the total m-power cost is at most C n^(m/2)h^(m−n), tending to zero. For any fixed scale δ>0, take h small enough that √n h≤δ; the grid is then a Nat-indexed δ-cover, after appending empty sets, with cost arbitrarily small. Thus C_m(E,δ)=0 for every δ>0, and the exact M008 formula H^m(E)=sup_{δ>0}C_m(E,δ) gives H^m(E)=0 for every m>n. The critical-exponent definition then yields D≤n. Fix arbitrary q>D; q>0. M003 at the NNReal coercion of q gives H^q(E)=0. Unfolding M008, H^q(E) is exactly the supremum over positive scales of the infimum of the Nat-indexed cover costs, so every scale content C_q(E,r)=0. For any r>0, cover E by open balls of radius r/3 and use compactness for a finite subcover; their diameters are ≤2r/3, giving an admissible Nat-indexed r-cover after appending empties. Thus the admissible class is nonempty, and for every γ>0 its infimum zero yields an r-cover of q-cost <γ. Choose r_j↓0, r_j≤1, and γ_j↓0 with such covers of cost <γ_j. Each nonempty zero-diameter member in Euclidean space is a singleton. Enumerate these by a finite or countable list and replace the k-th by an open ball containing it, of diameter ≤r_j and q-power cost <γ_j2^(−k−1); the total additional cost is <γ_j. Leave positive-diameter members and empty members unchanged. The resulting cover has all nonempty diameters d_i positive, d_i≤r_j, and q-cost <2γ_j. For each i partition [0,1] into N_i=⌈1/d_i⌉ closed intervals of length 1/N_i≤d_i; since d_i≤1, N_i≤1/d_i+1≤2/d_i. The products U_i×K_iℓ cover F, have diameter ≤√2d_i, and form a countable family (a countable union of finite families), which can be enumerated by ℕ with empty sets appended. Their total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)∑d_i^q<4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j, and their diameters are ≤√2r_j→0. For any fixed δ>0, all sufficiently large j have √2r_j≤δ; these product families are then admissible Nat-indexed δ-covers, so C_(q+1)(F,δ)≤4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j for all such j. Letting j→∞ gives C_(q+1)(F,δ)=0. This holds for every δ>0; the exact M008 supremum formula gives H^(q+1)(F)=0. M012 at NNReal exponent q+1 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since this holds for every q>D, density gives dim_H(F)≤D+1. For n=0, F is isometric to [0,1]; interval covers of mesh h have at most 1/h+1 members of diameter ≤h, whose total a-cost tends to zero for every a>1. The same M008 scale formula and M012 give dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Isometries preserve ediam, cover conditions and the exact M008 formula.
Set η_i=ε·2^(−i−1)/(1+ρ_i^s), interpreted using the underlying real value of the finite diameter ρ_i; thus η_i>0 and η_iρ_i^s≤ε·2^(−i−1).

For each i, if B_i is nonempty, choose an open interval J_i containing B_i whose length is at most diam(B_i)+η_i≤ρ_i+η_i, by enlarging its infimum/supremum enclosure by total width η_i. If B_i is empty, choose any open interval of length η_i; it contains B_i and satisfies the same bound.
